resolved_by: The Supreme Court resolved the split in Bowe v. United States, No. 24-5438, holding that 28 U.S.C. § 2244(b)(1)'s same-claim bar does not apply to federal prisoners filing second or successive § 2255 motions.
issue: Does the same-claim bar in 28 U.S.C. § 2244(b)(1) apply to federal prisoners seeking to file a second or successive motion under § 2255?

sides.position: Section 2244(b)(1)'s same-claim bar applies to federal prisoners' second or successive § 2255 motions, so previously raised claims must be dismissed.
cases: In re Michael Bowe, No. 24-11704 (11th Cir. 2026)

sides.position: Section 2244(b)(1) does not apply to federal prisoners; § 2255(h) incorporates only § 2244's certification procedures, so previously asserted claims may be brought again if they meet § 2255(h)'s requirements.

this_court: Follows the Supreme Court's rule in Bowe that § 2244(b)(1) does not apply to federal prisoners, and treats its own contrary Baptiste decision as abrogated.
quote: Addressing a circuit split about the applicability of § 2244(b)(1)’s sameclaim bar to federal prisoners, the Supreme Court abrogated our Baptiste decision.
cite: In re: Michael Bowe, No. 24-11704 (11th Cir. 2026)
